statement: The function returns a result r, and r is exactly the minimum possible largest segment sum for a split of nums into k non-empty contiguous subarrays. More precisely: (a) there exist integer indices 0 = p_0 < p_1 < ... < p_k = len(nums) such that, for every j with 0 <= j < k, the segment sum S_j = nums[p_j] + nums[p_j+1] + ... + nums[p_{j+1}-1] satisfies S_j <= r, and at least one such S_j equals r; and (b) for every choice of integer indices 0 = q_0 < q_1 < ... < q_k = len(nums), if T_j = nums[q_j] + ... + nums[q_{j+1}-1] for 0 <= j < k, then max_{0<=j<k} T_j >= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000; 1 <= k <= min(50, len(nums)).

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail: for every input satisfying the preconditions, there is no arithmetic overflow, no out-of-bounds indexing, and no panic.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000; 1 <= k <= min(50, len(nums)).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), r >= nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000; 1 <= k <= min(50, len(nums)).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if total = sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i], then k * r >= total. Equivalently, r is at least the smallest integer t such that k * t >= total (the ceiling of total/k).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000; 1 <= k <= min(50, len(nums)).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if total = sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i], then r <= total.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let P(p) = nums[0] + nums[1] + ... + nums[p-1] for 1 <= p <= len(nums), and let total = P(len(nums)). Then r = min { max(P(p), total - P(p)) | 1 <= p < len(nums) }.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000; 1 <= k <= min(50, len(nums)); k = 2.
